_comment: Device and LED inventory. Indices and names come from SimAppPro's www/js/DeviceConfig.js; part ids come from a broadcast ONLINE_HEARTBEAT. See docs/PROTOCOL.md.
_status: PTO2 and Orion Throttle Base II both fully verified 2026-09-16. Indices 0/1/2 are dimmers taking 0-255. Indices 4-17 are indicators taking 0 or 1 only; a value of 255 is out of range and is silently ignored (it acks, and nothing lights).

_evidence.dimmer: Indices 0, 1 and 2 observed taking 1, 2, 11, 13, 20, 22, 111, 137, 200, 222 and 255 from SimAppPro's sliders.
_evidence.indicator: SimAppPro only ever sends 0 or 1 to indices 4..17. Confirmed on hardware: 1 lights, 0 clears, 255 does nothing.
_evidence.hook_dimness: Index 17 (HOOK) is a physically dim lamp - visibly weaker than its neighbours even at full brightness. It is not a protocol difference.

_open_questions: The two devices differ here and it matters: on the PTO2, SL (index 2) at 0 COMPLETELY extinguishes indices 4-17 - it is a master gate. On the Orion II, Backlight (index 0) at 0 leaves A/A and A/G lit but very dim - it dims without gating. Reported by Cory from direct use of both panels; not yet isolated in a controlled test.

leds.note: Physically dim lamp; hard to see at distance. Not a protocol quirk.

_notes: Index 3 is absent from the vendor's own table. Not an omission here.
Indicators take 0 or 1. Writing 255 acks and does nothing - it is out of range, not truthy.
The 14 indicators match SimAppPro's UI list read top to bottom, which is how the index order was corroborated.

SL (index 2) is a MASTER GATE for indices 4-17: with SL at 0 no indicator lights at all, whatever value it is sent. This is stronger than the Orion II, where Backlight only dims. ENGINE CONSEQUENCE: a profile that binds any PTO2 indicator but leaves SL unbound must not have SL written to 0 by the module-load sweep, or every bound lamp is dead and acks normally while dark.

One USB interface, three parts, all answering a broadcast heartbeat. usb_pid 48484 (0xbd64) is the composite enumeration for base + these handles and changes if different handles are fitted, so parts are discovered rather than trusted from the PID.
Handle LED inventories are unknown and left empty rather than guessed.
Verified 2026-09-16 on hardware and against a SimAppPro HID capture. Index 0 is a dimmer; indices 1 and 2 are binary indicators - SimAppPro only ever sends 0 or 1 to them.

Index 0 (Backlight) governs the BRIGHTNESS of indices 1 and 2, but does not gate them: with Backlight at 0 the A/A and A/G lamps are still lit, just very dim. Brightness rises with Backlight. So a profile that binds A/A without binding Backlight yields a visible but very dim lamp, not a dead one.

Unlike the PTO2, this device LIGHTS an indicator when sent 255 rather than ignoring the out-of-range value. Brightness is identical at 1, 30 and 255 because the value is binary here and Backlight sets the level. Write 1, which is what the vendor sends.
SimAppPro does not clamp the Backlight field: entering 1255 transmitted 231 (0x4E7 truncated to its low byte 0xE7). That is a SimAppPro defect, not a device range.

_persisted_brightness.comment: SimAppPro writes the two PTO2 dimmers to device flash at config offset 0x114 as a little-endian word: byte 0 = Backlight, byte 1 = SL. Observed as '00 de 00 00' after SL=222 and '6f de 00 00' after Backlight=111.
_persisted_brightness.warning: We must never write this. WRITE_CFG_DATA is persistent and is on the forbidden list. Reading it with READ_CFG_DATA is safe and is how the daemon can warn when a user's stored brightness would make bound lamps invisible.
